title: Hunger Games fan, 13, to get artwork shown on cinema screens before film
content:
A teenage Hunger Games fan has met the cast of the new film after her artwork won a competition, meaning it will be displayed at every cinema screening across the UK.
Freja Brown, 13, won the British Board of Film Classification's (BBFC) create the card competition, which ran ahead of the release of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping - the sixth film in the franchise.
Freja, from Cardiff, beat more than 1,000 entries from across the UK and said she was "so grateful" to be chosen.
Her design will be the official BBFC black card, which displays the age rating and classification details of the film before every cinema showing.
The Year nine student, whose favourite subject is art, only started oil painting three years ago.
Her mum Marie recalled the moment Freja found out about the competition while scrolling on social media.
"She just squealed and said, 'there's this competition where you can create a piece of art' and she loves making art. So, she was like, 'I'm gonna do it'."
"She's read all the books and watched all the movies, so being able to combine her love for the Hunger Games with her own art sounded really fun."
Joseph Zada, Mckenna Grace, and Whitney Peak, who play Haymitch, Maysilee, and Lenore Dove in the new film, announced Freja's winning design in a specially recorded video.
Freja said: "I couldn't believe it. I knew that there were lots of other people who had sent in their artwork, so I didn't expect to be chosen and I am so grateful I was."
As part of her prize Freja was also invited to attend a screening of the film in London, where she met some of the stars.
Showing the work to Elle Fanning, who plays Effie Trinket, the actress said: "Oh my God, I thought it was a photo."
Actor Ralph Fiennes said: "It looks wonderful, it's really amazing, I love it."
Speaking of her inspiration, Freja said: "I was inspired by this specific part in the trailer because it shows the Hunger Games arena to be a beautiful place and not the killing machine that it actually is."
Marie, who is a photographer, said her daughter has always been a creative person and "makes stuff all the time", filling their home with her creations.
Marie said her daughter spent more than a month on the piece and worked until the day of the deadline after she "locked in for a whole weekend" to get it done.
She added that she was "so proud" of her daughter.
"It's not just a random piece of art somewhere, it's something that her and her friends get to see, which is fantastic."

final_quality.reason: While the article is lighthearted and fun, it provides a unique and inspiring story about a talented teenager, Freja Brown, who won a competition to have her artwork displayed on cinema screens before the release of The Hunger Games: Sunrise. The article offers a brief and sweet moment of triumph for the young artist, and readers may appreciate the enthusiasm and creativity of the 13-year-old. The story is not a routine celebrity update or trivial personal development, but rather a feel-good and uplifting tale that showcases the power of art and human connection.

title: Harry Styles, Billie Eilish, Sam Fender and Cher to headline Glastonbury 2027
content:
Harry Styles will make his Glastonbury festival debut next year as one of the event's headliners, alongside Sam Fender and Billie Eilish - with Cher among the other stars on the bill.
The veteran US pop icon will play the coveted Sunday afternoon "legends" slot, which is often considered a fourth headline set. It will be her only UK festival appearance of the year.
Other acts on the line-up include Sombr, Sienna Spiro, Lily Allen, The Streets, Chase & Status, Kacey Musgraves, Primal Scream and breakout pop star Adéla.
Tickets for the festival sold out in just 42 minutes last month , with demand particularly high after the event took a year off in 2026.
Electro pioneers Kraftwerk will make their Glastonbury debut with a headline set at West Holts - the festival's third-largest stage.
The event will also welcome experimental Canadian band Angine de Poitrine, who have drawn attention for their prog-rock sound and polka-dotted stage costumes; rap legends De La Soul and Mike D; and pop provocateur FKA Twigs.
"We are so happy to be coming back after our fallow year and, as we head into winter after that peaceful period, we wanted to give you an early musical taster of what's to come at Glastonbury 2027 with this spread of incredible artists," said organiser Emily Eavis.
"We can't wait to see you down here on Worthy Farm in June for some much-needed good times!"
The gates will open at Worthy Farm in Somerset to 200,000 fans on Wednesday 23 June, with music on the main stages kicking off on Friday 25 June.
Tickets prices are at an all-time high of £408, including a £5 booking fee per ticket.
Sam Fender will headline the first night, in what will be his second appearance at the festival.
He last played in 2022, immediately before Billie Eilish, and fought back tears as thousands of fans chanted along to hits like Seventeen Going Under and Hypersonic Missiles.
"Me and the boys have never been here before," he said. "We've never been here as punters, never played here before and we're doing that all in one day, which is the most crazy experience."
He will return as one of the UK's biggest rock stars, having won the Mercury Prize for his third album, People Watching, in 2025. Earlier this year, his duet with Olivia Dean - Rein Me In - became the UK's longest-running number one single of all time.
Fender is expected to release a new album ahead of his Glastonbury slot, which will land in the middle of his catchily-titled Proper Massive Stadium Tour.
Harry Styles will take the Pyramid Stage crown on the Saturday.
It comes amid acclaim for his euphoric and athletic Together Together tour, which largely focuses on the understated dance anthems of his fourth album Kiss All The Time. Disco Occasionally.
The pop star has previously been spotted partying at the festival's late-night dance arenas, despite attempting to go incognito in tracksuits and sunglasses.
In 2022, he was rumoured to be making a guest appearance during Eilish's set after his music was played during an early-morning soundcheck - but the duet never materialised.
Instead, Eilish gave a universally well-received performance, described as "imperious [and] hugely engaging" by the Guardian, and "proof that the future is here" by the NME .

final_quality.reason: Major entertainment development with a significant lineup of well-known artists, including Cher and Harry Styles' Glastonbury debut, making it a notable and newsworthy event.

title: Harry Potter to Pride and Prejudice: 10 of the best TV shows to watch this December
content:
From a new small screen adaptation of JK Rowling's mega-hit wizarding novels to Netflix's take on the Jane Austen classic – these are the best series to watch and stream.
Jed Mercurio, who created some of the best crime-and-suspense series of recent years, including Line of Duty and Bodyguard, is also behind this action-filled political thriller. Gugu Mbatha-Raw stars as Katherine Decker, second-in-command of a US nuclear submarine. Richard Madden is the US Secretary of Defense, Webb Preston. His name sounds made-for-TV but realism is probably not the point here. Preston is a slippery character, who wants Decker to trust him with a plan that she suspects might be a ruse. As Mercurio has put it , Preston "is either the saviour of world peace or its greatest threat". Mbatha-Raw (Surface and The Morning Show ) is great at displaying intensity and intelligence, and Madden (Bodyguard) is expert at playing smooth characters who keep us off-kilter, so the casting alone gives the series a good start.
Trinity premieres 1 December on Netflix internationally
The eight Harry Potter films had fairly long run times, at least two hours each, but HBO's ambitious new adaptation will give the stories even more room to breathe and to reach a generation that grew up on streaming. The series is eventually meant to adapt all seven novels, and in this first season Harry (Dominic McLaughlin, with an adorably innocent face) arrives at Hogwarts, where he meets Ron (Alastair Stout), Hermione (Arabella Stanton) and all those memorable teachers, friends and enemies. John Lithgow plays Dumbledore, Janet McTeer is Minerva McGonagall, Nick Frost is Hagrid and Paapa Essiedu has the juicy role of Severus Snape. Daniel Radcliffe, the original Harry, has welcomed the generational shift for his own reasons. "I'm delighted that when my kid grows up and is into Harry Potter he can watch a version that is not me," he has said .
Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone premieres 25 December on HBO and HBO Max in the US and Now/HBO Max in the UK
In 1995, the glorious BBC take on Pride and Prejudice – the one with Colin Firth in his wet shirt – set off a wave of Jane Austen adaptations. This latest version comes with a delightful new cast, with Jack Lowden as Darcy, Emma Corrin as Elizabeth and Daryl McCormack as Bingley. But the trailer also makes it look as if the Bennet sisters' parents, played by Olivia Colman and Rufus Sewell, might steal every scene. That fits with what Dolly Alderton, the novelist and memoirist (Everything I Know About Love) who wrote the series, has envisaged. Mrs Bennet, far from being the annoying mother she is often depicted as, is actually "the hero" according to Alderton . She says she "really felt I'd like justice for Mrs Bennet", whose matchmaking is an attempt to save her daughters from penniless futures. In another fresh tweak, here the dastardly seducer Wickham (Louis Partridge) catches Elizabeth's eye as well as her sister Lydia's. "I really need to fool the audience into thinking that he's the guy that Lizzie should be with," Alderton said, teasing how different her take might be on one of the best-known stories in the world.
Pride and Prejudice premieres 3 December on Netflix internationally
How many murders can happen in one Manhattan apartment building? Not enough to sustain this long-running charmer of a comedy, which has shrewdly changed strategies to stay fresh. Even the show's official Instagram account calls this sixth season Only Murders in London. This time Charles, Oliver and Mabel, the trio of unlikely crime-solving podcasters played by Steve Martin, Martin Short and Selena Gomez, investigate what happened to their podcasting rival Cinda Canning (Tina Fey), found dead outside the gates of their murder building at the end of last season. The trail takes them to London and ramps up the series' other strategy for staying fresh – bringing in A-list guest stars. Meryl Streep returns as Oliver's wife, and is joined by a dream lineup of actors including David Tennant, Olivia Colman, Martin Freeman, Nicola Coughlan and Richard E Grant. And that's just a partial list of additions to this much-anticipated new case.
Only Murders in the Building premieres 8 December on Hulu in the US and Disney+ in the UK
Ever since the 1996 murder of the six-year-old beauty pageant winner JonBenét Ramsey, whose body was found in the basement of her family's home in Boulder, Colorado, that unsolved case has never quite left public view. The child's smiling photos, her family's well-off status and some mysterious clues like a kidnapping note created a story ready-made for intense scrutiny and for the screen. The past decades have produced a raft of documentaries and dramas about the killing, but no previous drama has featured such a high-powered cast, with Melissa McCarthy as JonBenét's mother, Patsy, and Clive Owen as her father, John. Public suspicion has long been directed their way, but they have steadfastly insisted on their innocence, and they were cleared by prosecutors in 2008 , based on DNA evidence. (Patsy died in 2006.) Richard LaGravanese, writer of The Fisher King and the series Behind the Candelabra, is behind the show, which goes back before the murder and onto the investigation into what has become one of the most famous of all true-crime stories.
The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey premieres 10 December on Netflix internationally
There can never be enough Jane Austen on TV, if the series are done as well as this enormously popular period piece , a spin-off from Pride and Prejudice focusing on the neglected middle Bennet sister. In the first season, the bookish Mary (Ella Bruccoleri) arrived in London and made what was obviously the right choice of suitors, picking the poetic Tom Hayward (Donal Finn) over his rival for her affections, the adventurous William Ryder (Laurie Davidson). This three-part holiday special picks up a year into the Haywards' marriage, with Mary trying to fit her independent spirit into the 19th-Century's cookie-cutter idea of a good wife. "They are completely in love, still, the soppy pair!" Bruccoleri told Radio Times about Tom and Mary. But, she added, even with that "perfect fairy tale" of a marriage, "ultimately you're expected to become this thing that might not fit naturally with who you are," which leaves Mary spending far too much time making jam. Ruth Jones returns as Mrs Bennet, along with Davidson as Ryder and Tanya Reynolds (Coach Chilton on Ted Lasso) as the snobbish Caroline Bingley.
The Other Bennet Sister premieres December on the BBC in the UK and Britbox in the US
Jhumpa Lahiri's 2008 short story collection inspired this drama, which brings together characters who never met in the book, but who are all part of the Indian diaspora in the US. Freida Pinto plays Parul Chaudhury, whose cancer diagnosis sends her, along with her husband and their teenage son, from Mumbai back to Cambridge, Massachusetts for treatment. It's a place where she spent some of her happiest years, at Harvard, and also where her long-lost love, Amit Mukherjee (Siddharth) still lives. When they reconnect, it's the catalyst for a melodramatic plot that involves their families, including Parul's son. Madhuri Shekar, the showrunner, has said : "So much of what we talked about in the writers' room is what it’s like growing up as children, knowing that there are affairs happening between the adults and nobody's talking about it." And Pinto added that they are hoping it offers a very different depiction of South Asian mothers "and not the typical strict parenting that we've seen over and over again".
Unaccustomed Earth premieres 17 December on Netflix internationally
Samuel L Jackson stars in this crime comedy, the latest series created and written by Taylor Sheridan, who must be setting some sort of record for making shows with big-name actors. This one is spun off from Sheridan's Tulsa King, in which Sylvester Stallone plays a crime boss in Oklahoma. Jackson plays Russell Lee Washington, known as Lee, a former mob hitman introduced in Tulsa King, when he was sent to kill Stallone's character but refused to go through with the job. Seems it's hard to kill your old prison buddy. Now Lee is setting up his own operation in Frisco, Texas, surrounding himself with a new crew of willing misfits. "This feels pretty criminal," one person says in the trailer , and Lee responds "And?", shrugging it off with perfect drollness. Stallone will make guest appearances in a couple of episodes, but Jackson alone is more than enough.
Frisco King premieres 18 December on Paramount+ in the US and UK
Emily is calling it quits, from the series if not necessarily from Paris. Whether she stays in her adopted city or not is the big question in this sixth and final season. Before she decides, though, the story takes her to Greece and to Monaco, and brings Gabriel (Lucas Bravo), one of her most important exes, back into her life. Alongside Emily (Lily Collins), her best friend Mindy (Ashley Park) has to make some romantic choices of her own. And we'll see what happens at Agence Grateau, the marketing agency that brought Emily to Paris in the first place. Philippine Leroy-Beaulieu returns as the company's chic owner, Sylvie, with Minnie Driver as the scheming Princess Jane. It's hard to imagine that the show will give the characters anything but a happy ending, with glamorous locations and fashions no one would wear in real life – the very fantasies that have made Emily such a long-running hit.
Emily in Paris premieres 24 December on Netflix internationally
Fifteen seasons into its run, this beloved series is looking back at the early days of some favourite characters in a three-part prequel set during World War Two. The location is the same London neighbourhood where the midwives work, this time under the threat of bombing during the Blitz and shortages that make their jobs more difficult than ever. Jenny Agutter, Sister Julienne in the main series, is the narrator, with new actors playing younger versions of Julienne (Helena Wilson), Sister Monica-Joan (Helen Schlesinger) and Sister Evangeline (Amy Booth-Steel). Heidi Thomas, who created the original, has also done the prequel. When it was announced, she said : "It is about love and birth, separation and courage, lipstick and nylons (or the lack thereof). But it is also a medical drama, set in a devastating landscape where even the nurses cannot know if they will live till morning."
